key_insight: Two structure-preserving discretisations generate entropy and enforce quasi-incompressibility pointwise, while only the continuous Petrov–Galerkin method also conserves total energy.
engineering_relevance: These methods support physically consistent simulation of coupled heat transfer, multicomponent diffusion, and fluid motion in miscible mixtures.
method: Model thermal Maxwell–Stefan–Navier–Stokes dynamics using mass, momentum, and entropy balances.
Combine semi-implicit Euler time stepping with suitable spatial finite elements.
Use continuous Petrov–Galerkin time discretisation for energy conservation and high-order temporal approximation.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments demonstrate the structure-preserving properties and behaviour of both methods; the abstract reports no quantitative accuracy or efficiency metrics.
watch_item: The semi-implicit Euler method numerically dissipates total energy, which may matter for long-time thermal simulations.
paper_title: Structure-preserving discretisations for the quasi-incompressible, thermal Maxwell-Stefan equations
